fact: In 2005, my galleries hosted 21 exhibitions. The flagship exhibition was 'Hatched: National Graduate Show 2005' (showcasing 60 emerging artists). Other major exhibitions that year were Shiro Takatani's media installations (as part of the Japan-Australia exchange RAPT! project), Richard Giblett's work in the 'New Dystopias' group show, and photographer Tony Nathan's solo exhibition 'Proof of Light' (October 20 – November 13, 2005).

In 2005, PICA's CEO and Director was Sarah Miller. Hannah Mathews served as a key curator on my team (starting her curatorial tenure at PICA from 2005 to 2008), shaping the year's experimental visual arts program alongside guest curators.

Artists who exhibited in 2005 include photographer Tony Nathan (solo exhibition 'Proof of Light'), Shiro Takatani (media arts), Richard Giblett (New Dystopias), and Hatched graduates Tom Halliday, Natalie Preiato, Shannon Lyons, Keumhee Oh, Stephanie Hicks, Alex James, Paul Wotherspoon, Joanne Gerke, Rebecca Jones, and Ryan Nazzari.

My history features key directors: Noel Sheridan (founding director, 1989-1993) who set my experimental and multidisciplinary tone; Sarah Miller (1993-2006) who expanded national presence; Amy Barrett-Lennard (2006-2022) who focused on residency commissions; and Hannah Mathews (2022-Present) who Curates research-driven collaborations. Sarah Wall is currently the Curator.

In 2005, I hosted 13 performance works. My long history of performance includes Joan Jonas' mirror performance 'Mirror Piece I & II' (restaged in 2024 for Bunuru season/Perth Festival), Cassils' performance 'Becoming an Image' in their ALCHEMIC show, Amrita Hepi's 'Monumental' choreographic video work, Laure Prouvost (2025), and Francesca Lasica's 'WHEN I AM NOT THERE' season.

PICA Bar & Cafe operates on my front ground-floor verandah, serving as a popular social hub in the Perth Cultural Centre where artists, curators, and visitors gather for drinks, coffee, and discussions.

I was designed in 1896 in the Federation Free Classical style by architect George Temple Poole, featuring red face-brick, stucco details, a central double-height hall, and a signature landmark clock tower on James Street.

Architects Donaldson and Warn designed my major refurbishment in 1991, converting the former segregated boys' school layout into galleries and a performance space, officially opening as PICA on November 8, 1991.

Opened in 1897 as the Perth Boys' and Girls' School (part of the Perth Central School complex). It was segregated, with boys on the ground floor and girls on the first floor. From 1959 to 1988, I was a branch of Perth Technical College (TAFE) before becoming PICA in 1989.

My signature visual art programs include 'Hatched: National Graduate Show' (annual flagship since 1992 showcasing visual arts graduates) and the Judy Wheeler Commission (annual site-specific visual arts commission activating my front lobby and glass facade).
From April 18 to June 14, 2026, my galleries hosted 'Revealed: New and Emerging WA Aboriginal Artists' (showcasing new WA Aboriginal artists) and Dellas Bennell's 'Where Waters Meet' in my PICA Hub.

In July 2026, I hosted the contemporary dance show 'Restore' by STRUT Dance (July 15-18, 2026) accompanied by post-show artist talks featuring Ainslie Allen, Annika Moses, Brooke Stamp, and Daniel Jenatsch. I also hosted 'On Labour: Four Live Works' (July 2-4, 2026) featuring live works by Grace Connors, Barbara Hostalek, Sukhjit Kaur Khalsa, and Sarah Rodigari.

In mid-2026, my studio spaces hosted numerous resident artists, including Benjamin Quirk (Quick Response, July 13-26), Kumo-bako/Ken Meyer (Quick Response, June 15 - July 5), Lauren Jane Salt (Quick Response, June 15 - July 5), Maraya Takoniatis (Quick Response, June 1-14), Mohammed 'Ayo Busari' with blue joy theatre company (May 25 - June 14), Naoko Uemoto for the BREEZE Perth-Makassar International Exchange Residency (May 11 - June 7), Germaine Chan (May 4-24), Liv McIntyre (May 4-31), and Grace Connors for Bluebird23 (May 2 - June 21).

My 2026 public program featured diverse events, including the Reconciliation Week: Revealed In Conversation panel (May 30, 2026), the First Nations Curating Panel (June 11, 2026) with curators Glenn Iseger-Pilkington and Ilona McGuire, a film screening of 'Dungku Asang' (May 2, 2026), the Open Studios: Djeran showcase (April 29, 2026), and hand block printing workshops led by Nagula Jarndu (April 18, 2026).

Regarding my about: Over its 30 plus-year history, PICA has operated as both a producing and presenting organisation, delivering an annual program of changing exhibitions, seasons in contemporary dance, experimental theatre, new music and live art as well as a range of artist-in-residence programs.
Regarding my about: PICA works with artists who are trail-blazers, exemplars, innovators and change-makers, and acts as a site for challenging and timely conversations.

Regarding my about: Its programs are carefully crafted, ensuring connections are forged not only between artists and audiences but across art forms, cultures and geographies. For artists, audiences and other communities it serves, PICA is a meeting place, a provocateur, a resource and most importantly a partner in the realisation of big and new ideas.
Regarding my about: Visionary Thinking – We work with artists at the forefront of culture and ideas, encouraging experimentation, innovation, free-thinking and fresh voices.
Regarding my about: Connection – We support artists to create enriching and thought-provoking experiences that connect with diverse communities.
Regarding my about: Pathways – We work with artists and arts workers at all stages of their careers, creating opportunities that respond to their needs and sustain their practice.

Regarding my about: Belonging – We are committed to building a supportive environment of integrity and accountability where people feel seen, heard and supported. Working together is central to everything we do.
Regarding my about: Sustainability – We collectively imagine and contribute to a sustainable and more equitable future for the arts, and society more broadly.

Regarding my about: Housed in a large and striking heritage building in the Perth Cultural Centre , Western Australia, PICA was incorporated in 1989 but its emergence was preceded by the commitment and hard work undertaken over five years by its founders. Securing PICA’s eventual location, in what was originally the Perth Central School, was fundamental to that process.

Regarding my about: The new organisation partly ‘follow[ed] on from Praxis (Western Australia’s former Contemporary Art Space now amalgamated with PICA), which had a 15-year history of producing an important program of visual arts exhibitions, publications and special projects. Praxis had been a part of a network of contemporary art spaces across Australia; organisations which had their origins in the alternative spaces of the 1970s, and which at their best were critical, challenging and provocative.

Regarding my about: The intention of those people and groups involved in the development of the Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts was that it would provide a new forum for the analysis and presentation of critical and contemporary art practice. This practice would include the visual arts, music, dance and performance along with their contemporary and interdisciplinary variants but would be wider than any list of art forms… Fundamental to the concept of PICA was that culture was not an isolated province but intimately connected to the social, economic, psychological and political dimensions of contemporary life.’ 1

Regarding my about: The late Noel Sheridan was the inaugural Director of PICA from 1989–93. During this time he put his vision into action by delivering a dynamic program and overseeing the initial renovation of the building that PICA still calls home. He was succeeded by Sarah Miller, who from 1993–2006 continued PICA’s development into one of the country’s most innovative, best-known and loved contemporary arts venues in Australia. In 2006, Amy Barrett-Lennard was appointed as Director. She led the evolution of PICA until August 2022, responding to the changing needs and desires of artists and audiences with the ultimate goal of forging an inclusive space that sits at the nexus of art, innovation and community. In October 2022, Hannah Mathews joined PICA as its new CEO.

Regarding my about: Sarkis Akopov – Board Member Sarkis Akopov is a motivated and enthusiastic leader. With his positive attitude and collaborative approach, he has earned the trust of colleagues and clients alike. Sarkis’s strength lies in his logical and analytical mindset, coupled with his exceptional numerical skills. He is constantly seeking new challenges and opportunities to enhance his expertise in areas such as strategic planning, financial analysis, change management, IFRS, and US GAAP. His dedication to his craft is evident in the exceptional results he consistently delivers.

Regarding my about: Clothilde Bullen, OAM – Board Member Clothilde Bullen OAM is a Wardandi (Noongar) and Badimaya (Yamatji) woman, curator, writer and advocate whose work has shaped contemporary Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts practice in Australia. She is currently Manager, ECU Art, Culture and Collections at Edith Cowan University, where she leads the development and stewardship of the University’s cultural assets. Previously, she was Lead, Cultural Strategy and Development, where she finalised ECU’s Cultural Narrative strategy. Before joining ECU, Bullen held senior curatorial roles at the Art Gallery of Western Australia and the Museum of Contemporary Art Australia, where she was the inaugural Senior Curator of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Collections and Exhibitions. Her award-winning exhibitions include Richard Bell: You Can Go Now and John Mawurndjul: I am the old and the new . Bullen has held many board and advisory roles, including Chair of the National Association for the Visual Arts and the Australian chapter of the International Association of Art Critics. She has published widely, co-edited Artlink and championed pathways for First Nations writers and arts workers. In 2025, she was awarded a Medal of the Order of Australia for service to the arts, particularly Indigenous arts.

Regarding my about: Minali Gamage – Board Member Minali Gamage is a governance, risk and audit professional with 18 years’ experience working primarily with critical infrastructure and global mining companies, both as a management consultant and in-house. Minali regularly supports the arts through advocacy, philanthropy, arts advisory roles, and collecting. She is the founder of perth.art.seeker, a social media-based information-sharing service about art exhibitions, events, and industry opportunities in and around Perth.\

Regarding my about: Dr Andrew Lu, AM – Chair Dr Andrew Lu AM is President of the Mental Health Tribunal, Chair of PICA and Australian Baroque, and a non-executive director of SBS, Melbourne International Film Festival, and the Australian Youth Orchestra. His 30 years of governance experience includes board roles with the Arts Law Centre of Australia, National Gallery of Australia Foundation, Jigsaw, Chamber of Arts and Culture WA, AGWA Foundation, and the Canberra Symphony Orchestra. A graduate of UWA Law School with a research Doctorate in Law from ANU and a Master of Laws from New England, he was a litigation partner and solicitor in private practice with global and Australian law firms for 21 years. He also served on the State Administrative Tribunal and the Reproductive Technology Council. An Adjunct Professor of Curtin Law School, he is a Fellow of the Australian Institute of Company Directors and the Australian Academy of Law. An arts and inclusion advocate, he was named a Member of the Order of Australia in 2021.

Regarding my about: Hannah Mathews – Board Member Hannah Mathews is the Director/CEO of the Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts (PICA). Over the last twenty years, she has held key curatorial positions at Monash University Museum of Art, Australian Centre for Contemporary Art, Next Wave, The South Project and the Biennale of Sydney. Hannah graduated with a Master of Art Curatorship from the University of Melbourne in 2002 and has completed curatorial residencies in New York, Berlin, Tokyo and Venice. She has taught in curatorial programs at Melbourne University, Monash University and RMIT University, Melbourne and has held various board positions, including National Association for the Visual Arts, City of Melbourne Arts & Culture and International Art Space, Perth. Her publication, To Note: Notation Across Disciplines won the inaugural Cornish Family Book Prize for Art and Design Publishing in 2018.

Regarding my about: Jeremy Smith – Board Member Jeremy Smith is arts leader with more than 25 years’ experience across Australia’s creative industries. He has held senior roles with DADAA Inc, the Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts and Performing Lines WA, and spent nearly a decade in government arts funding with Creative Australia and ArtsWA. A WAAPA graduate, he began his career in production before moving into leadership, policy and community engagement. Since May 2025, Jeremy has been Head of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging at APM. Proudly identifying as a queer, disabled man, Jeremy brings a deep commitment to intersectionality, equity and self-determination. He has led initiatives supporting disability arts, young people, regional communities and First Nations-led practice. He serves on the boards of ArtsPay Foundation, chairs pvi collective and contributed to Equity: The National Arts and Disability Associated Plan.

Regarding my about: Saffron Solomon – Board Member Saffron Solomon is a marketing and communications specialist with over 25 years’ experience across the human services, finance, insurance, arts and energy sectors. Passionate about working with organisations that drive leadership, impact and positive change, she is a long-time advocate for people with disability and a dedicated supporter of Western Australia’s arts and culture community. With expertise spanning marketing strategy and management, business growth and development, Saffron is currently General Manager, Marketing at APM – a global human services provider dedicated to enabling better lives through a network of more than 14,000 people across 11 countries. She also serves on the Boards of the Guildford Grammar Foundation and Solomon Hollett Lawyers and has previously held board roles with Artrage, and director roles with Interchange and Block Branding.

Regarding my about: Paula Taylor – Board Member Paula Taylor began her career in London by fundraising for the arts at the Royal Court Theatre and the Royal Academy of the Arts before becoming Awards Director at D&AD (Design and Art Direction). With over a decade at D&AD – a global non-profit dedicated to creative excellence – she led strategic initiatives across multiple continents, collaborating with leading advertising creatives, designers, filmmakers, technologists and brands. As co-founder of West Tech Fest and First NationsX, Paula is dedicated to fostering innovation, equality, diversity and social impact. She is a graduate of Curtin University and the Victorian College of the Arts.

Regarding my about: Melvin Yeo – Board Member Melvin Yeo is a company director and corporate lawyer with more than 25 years’ experience. He has a global client base, and has also co-founded various international mineral exploration projects. Melvin’s experience includes governance, strategic planning, legal affairs, capital raising, operational oversight and transaction negotiations. Melvin is a supporter of the arts and is a Trustee of the WA State Government’s Arts and Culture Trust. He is also a keen collector of contemporary works by Australian artists and has previously served on the Murdoch University Art Collection board. Melvin was also a co-founder and board member of Heritage Perth Inc.

Regarding my about: Our Aboriginal Advisory Group is made up of leading Aboriginal visual and performing artists and arts workers: Sharyn Egan, Stephen Gilchrist, Glenn Iseger-Pilkington, Rohin Kickett and Janine Oxenham.

Regarding my about: By forming an Aboriginal Advisory Group, PICA seeks to embed the voices and cultural protocols of First Nations artists into the words and actions of what we do. PICA recognises the rights of First Nations people to oversee the representation of their diverse cultures. First Nations programming at PICA must therefore be First Nations-led.

Regarding my about: Sharyn Egan Sharyn Egan is a Noongar woman who began creating art at the age of 37, which lead to her enrolling in a Diploma of Fine Arts at the Claremont School of Art in Perth. She completed this course in 1998 and enrolled in the Associate Degree in Contemporary Aboriginal Art at Curtin University, which she completed in 2000. In 2001 she was awarded a Bachelor of Arts (Arts) from Curtin University. She has also been awarded a Certificate VI in Training and Education in 2011. The themes in Egan’s work are informed by the experiences of her life as a Noongar woman.

Regarding my about: Stephen Gilchrist Belonging to the Yamatji people of the Inggarda language group of northwest Western Australia, Dr Stephen Gilchrist is a Senior Lecturer in the School of Indigenous Studies at The University of Western Australia. He is a writer and curator who has worked with the Indigenous Australian collections of the National Gallery of Australia, British Museum, National Gallery of Victoria and Hood Museum of Art, Dartmouth College (2011–2013). Gilchrist has curated numerous exhibitions in Australia and the United States and has written extensively on Indigenous Art from Australia. 2012–2016, he was the Australian Studies Visiting Curator at the Harvard Art Museums, Harvard University.

Regarding my about: Glenn Iseger-Pilkington Glenn Iseger-Pilkington (Nhanda and Noongar Peoples/Dutch/Scottish) is a curator, cultural strategist, writer and senior arts manager with more than 20 years of experience across visual arts, cultural leadership, community engagement and national advocacy. Glenn’s career spans senior positions at Fremantle Arts Centre, Western Australian Museum, Art Gallery of Western Australia, South Australian Museum, national First Nations visual arts initiatives and major government cultural projects in Western Australia.

Regarding my about: Rohin Kickett Rohin Kickett is a Balardong, Whadjuk Noongar artist born in Northam, Western Australia 1986. He spent his childhood years in Gosnells and now resides in Armadale, where he has been a full-time practising artist since 2017. Before becoming an artist, Kickett had completed an apprenticeship in Metal Fabrication and 1st Class Welding, where he spent 12 years in the metal fabrication industry. At 32, Rohin completed the Indigenous Tertiary Enabling Course at the Centre for Aboriginal Studies at Curtin University. Over the last six years, Kickett has participated in many exhibitions, held solo exhibitions, completed a residency along with international cultural exchange programs, and completed multiple public art projects.

Regarding my about: Janine Oxenham Janine Oxenham is a Malgana Yamatji woman from the Shark Bay area in WA. She has studied dance at both NAISDA College, NSW and WAAPA, WA. She has choreographed and performed as a freelance contemporary Indigenous dancer for numerous festivals in regional WA. In 2015 she mounted the work Willy Willy as part of the Ausdance’s Future Landings project. She has facilitated community dance groups and performed as part of the core crew for the travelling festival Creality (formerly Gascoyne in May) for the past nine years. More recently, Oxenham has worked as Movement Director and choreographer for Yirra Yaakin and Perth Festival productions of Hecate and Panawathi Girl.

Regarding my about: Initiated in 2023, PICA’s Artist Advisory Group includes a panel of artists from across art forms and generations who work together to advise PICA on matters of importance to artists. Chaired by the current artist member of the PICA Board, the group is committed to including diverse experiences and perspectives and advocating for the needs of artists and the community.

Regarding my about: Nazerul Ben-Dzulkefli Nazerul Ben-Dzulkefli is a Singapore-born artist based in Boorloo (Perth), primarily working with ceramics. His practice sits between tradition and experimentation, often shaped by stories, languages and cultural fragments carried across seas, while being grounded in making, ritual practices, Malay myths and cosmologies. Ben-Dzulkeflihas presented work in various group exhibitions in Boorloo since 2017. He was selected as one of twenty-five most notable Australian art graduates of 2021 and was part of the Hatched: National Graduate Exhibition 2022 at Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts. Currently working as a Visual Art Technician at a K-12 school, he has also exhibited in the State Library of Western Australia, ECU’s Spectrum Project Space, Gallery Central, Stala Contemporary, Lawson Flats, Sweet Pea Arts, Gotham Artist Studios’ Peek-a-Boo micro gallery space, and Starch in Singapore.

Regarding my about: Sam Bloor Sam Bloor is a visual artist from Boorloo (Perth). Bloor’s background as a traditional signwriter informs his use of text provocations both in gallery spaces and site-specific public artworks. A thematic underpinning of Bloor’s work is exploring the ways in which language is filtered through personal experience generating malleable outcomes of meanings from a single prompt. Bloor holds a Bachelor of Arts (Fine Art) from Curtin University and has exhibited in a number of group and solo shows both nationally and internationally including, Totem In Tribute , Edinburgh, UK (2016), The Fremantle Biennale (2019; 2023; 2025), Rotterdam Photo Festival, The Netherlands (2019). He was commissioned to produce a major public work as part of Perth Festival (2022) and travelled to Venice as a drawing technician on Kith and Kin —Archie Moore work that was awarded the Golden Lion at the 2024 Venice Biennale.

Regarding my about: Kristen Brownfield Kristen Brownfield is an artist and artsworker living in Boorloo (Perth). Through artmaking, Kristen explores relationships to time, materials, memory, place and the environments in which we are entangled. Her work unfolds through observation and listening, is often temporal in nature or site-related, composed of found objects, photography, sound and video, writing and drawing. She holds a Bachelor of Arts (Visual Arts) from Edith Cowan University and a Bachelor of Arts (Fine Art, Honours) from RMIT University. Brownfield currently works with ART ON THE MOVE, where she coordinates the Artist in Residence program, supporting artists to undergo residencies in regional WA.

Regarding my about: Jo Darbyshire Jo Darbyshire is a visual artist living in Walyalup (Fremantle). Primarily a painter, she works across a variety of platforms in the arts. Jo’s abstract paintings often explore a strong relationship with the WA coast, her interest in its underwater landscapes and traces of colonial life. In other projects – including the ‘Gay Museum’ at the WA Museum (2003) and her artist-in-residence collaboration with Nyoongar artist Andrea Williams in Lake Grace as part of SPACED’s Rural Utopias program (2023) – she incorporates ideas about the archive and contemporary social history. Jo holds a Master of Creative Arts in Cultural Heritage from Curtin University (2004) and exhibits with Art Collective WA.

Regarding my about: Jensine Datu Jensine Datu is an Australian-Filipinx early career artist living and working on Whadjuk Noongar country. Their interdisciplinary practice draws on their personal experiences and everyday observations to highlight and observe underlying structures of hierarchy, power dynamics and hidden trauma. Through repetition and subversion, they process the emergence of intuitive self-healing in their work. In 2019 they graduated with a Bachelor of Fine Art from Curtin University and have been involved in group exhibitions at Cool Change Contemporary, Pig Melon and The Substation. They have undertaken residencies with Nod Space, Fremantle Arts Centre, Cool Change Contemporary and is currently taking part in Next Wave’s Kickstart Program.

Regarding my about: Emma Fishwick Emma Fishwick is a choreographer based in Boorloo (Perth), with an interdisciplinary practice that works across movement, digital media, writing, textiles and academic scholarship. Emma has worked extensively across Australia and abroad, lectures in Politics of Dance, Choreography, and is an Honours supervisor at Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts (WAAPA). In 2024, Emma completed her PhD research, Slow Choreographies , which addressed everyday sexisms in Australian universities through embodied creative methods. In 2025, Emma is a recipient of a Minderoo Artist Residency and participated in the ATLAS choreographic program at ImpulsTanz, Vienna.

Regarding my about: Shanti Gelmi Incorporating installation, sculpture, print and drawing, Shanti Gelmi delves into the intricate dynamics of human connection, identity and behaviour. Her works blend conceptual and process-driven techniques as she explores form and structure as a metaphor for interconnected existences, memory and experience. A first generation Australian of Indian migrants, Shanti often focuses on the struggle to preserve cultural heritage while assimilating into Australian society. She has a Bachelor of Contemporary Arts from Edith Cowan and is represented in the University’s Art Collection. Shanti was commissioned by Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts to develop her installation ‘Shadowed’ into a Virtual Reality experience in 2022, and her work is published in national and international art publications.

Regarding my about: Beverley Iles Beverley Iles is a sculpture-based artist whose work examines the essence of place: how we make sense of what is around us, how we form connections with a site and how we live together in a literal and existential sense. As a migrant and adoptee, Isles is interested in belonging, stability, construction of personal permanence and the complexities of coexistence. The frequent use of site-specific and found materials act to document a site but often disrupt identification with place. Isles holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from Curtin University and has undertaken a number of residencies, been part of a collaborative project with a Taiwanese curator and featured in a documentary about working cross culturally, has been selected for a sculpture scholarship and residency in Switzerland, and has exhibited in numerous group exhibitions in Melbourne, Brisbane and Western Australia.

Regarding my about: Cass Lynch Cass Lynch is a Koreng, Wudjari and Noongar woman and a descended from the families of Ravensthorpe in the Great Southern region. She is a writer and Research Fellow at Curtin University and has a PhD that explores Noongar stories that reference climate change. Cass is a member of the Wirlomin Noongar Language and Stories group who focus on the revitalisation of culture and language connected to south coast Noongar people. She has published short stories, essays and poems, and her multimedia storytelling works have been featured at Perth Festival, Fremantle Biennale and more. Her Noongar language haikus won the 2019 Patricia Hackett Prize and her short story ‘Split’, a creative impression of deep time Perth, can be found in the publication Flock: First Nations Stories Then and Now (University QLD Press, 2021) .

Regarding my about: Chloe Ogilvie Chloe Ogilvie is a Yamatji Nanda woman from Western Australia, where she graduated from the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts specialising in Lighting Design. Chloe works mostly as a designer but has crossed over into other areas such as production management and event coordination. Chloe has been a resident artist with Black Swan for three years and is currently co-curating the Maali Festival. Chloe Ogilvie is also a member of the arts collective The Farm where she has designed and production managed a range of shows including Throttle, Cockfight (Drover Award Winner), Ninth Wave, TIDE (Helpmann Award Winner) and Depthless .

Regarding my about: Katt Osborne Katt Osborne is an award-winning director and performance-maker, based in Boorloo (Perth). Her work explores stories and concepts that are messy, imperfect, heightened, surreal, playful and underpinned by a strong sense of musicality. Katt’s work as an independent artist has included works in a range of forms, including devised contemporary performance, new writing, cross-artform and hybrid performance, and directing plays, opera and musical theatre. In addition to her creative practice, Katt is also an established arts leader. Most recently, she led The Blue Room Theatre through the pandemic as Executive Director. In 2023, Katt was awarded a prestigious WA Business News 40under40 Award for entrepreneurship in the arts and cultural sector. Tyrown Waigana Tyrown Waigana is a multidisciplinary artist and designer whose practice spans painting, illustration, sculpture, animation and graphic design. Of Wandandi Noongar, Yawuru and Ait Koedal heritage, Waigana was born in East Fremantle and raised in the surrounding suburbs of Western Australia. His work explores themes such as everyday myths, gaps in communication and the rhetoric surrounding Indigenous identity—often infused with wit and humour. Through his art, Waigana seeks to challenge perceptions while embracing opportunities that push creative boundaries, allowing him to continually evolve and grow as an artist. Waigana holds a Bachelor of Fine Art from Curtin University, runs Crawlin Crocodile, an art and design service, and has exhibited work with the Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts and Fremantle Art Centre.

Regarding my about: Past members of PICA’s Artist Advisory Group include Kieron Broadhurst, Erin Coates, kelli mccluskey, Ilona McGuire, Renée Newman, Rachel Arianne Ogle, Joshua Pether and Andrew Varano.

Our welcoming gallery environment celebrates diversity, free from discrimination and harassment for people of all lived experiences.

Regarding my access: Increasing access to and participation in arts and culture is one of our central aims. The Social Model of Disability informs what we do, seeing people as being disabled by barriers in society rather than by their differences. We recognise that disability is one aspect of a person’s life and does not determine who they are.

Regarding my access: Disability may not always be visible, and we aim to remove barriers for people living with memory loss, along with sensory and mental health conditions. PICA offers a range of facilities and services to meet peoples’ access needs and works closely with community and access partners to deliver supported programs for diverse audiences and under-represented groups. If you have any access questions please contact us at info@pica.org.au or (08) 9228 6300
Regarding my access: Our step-by-step visual and written guide for visitors let’s you know how to find PICA and what to expect on your visit.
Regarding my access: PICA offers a range of events tailored to specific access needs. Our events include quiet hours, tactile tours, Auslan-interpreted artist talks and more.
Regarding my access: PICA provides services to increase participation and access to our programs and facilities.
Regarding my access: At PICA access is a core part of professional working conditions. PICA is committed to making our programs and application processes as accessible as possible for artists.

As the only survey exhibition of its kind in Australia, Hatched has become a much-anticipated program for artists and audiences alike, reinforcing PICA’s unwavering commitment to supporting new generations of leading contemporary artists.

Regarding my hatched: Since its inception in 1992, Hatched has featured the work of over 1,400 artists, serving as a crucial platform for early-career artists in Australia. Hatched was conceived by PICA’s inaugural director, Noel Sheridan, and focussed on presenting a large, diverse survey of work from art school graduates across the country. Following its early years, Hatched was refined and given its now-iconic title by PICA’s second director, Sarah Miller. For many, Hatched marks their first opportunity to exhibit at a major arts institution, introducing their work to a national audience. In addition to the exhibition, PICA offers a bespoke professional development program for the selected artists shaped with and in response to their practices and needs. Along with an annual exhibition catalogue, Hatched also offers two studio residencies each year: one for an interstate artist and one for a WA-based artist to spend time at PICA to develop new projects.

Regarding my hatched: In recent years, Hatched has been led by the appointment of a Hatched Curatorial Associate—a position designed to support the career of an emerging curator. This initiative has been made possible by the foresight and generous support of Minderoo Foundation. Offering a rare opportunity for an emerging curator to lead a large-scale, multi-faceted exhibition such as Hatched, the Curatorial Associate works to provide dedicated support and attention to each exhibiting artist while being mentored by the PICA team. In 2021-2022 Miranda Johnson was appointed as the inaugural Curatorial Associate and was succeeded by Brent Harrison, who held the role in 2023-24. Mia Palmer-Verevis takes on the curatorial leadership of Hatched for 2025-2026.

Regarding my hatched: The Schenberg Arts Awards, established in 2009, are a cornerstone of the support that Hatched offers emerging artists. These awards offer substantial prize money to encourage the development of emerging practice and allow new artists to further invest in the progression of their career. These awards, now totalling a generous $50,000, are made possible by the Dr Harold Schenberg Bequest and presented in partnership with the University of Western Australia. Over the past 15 years, the Schenberg Arts Awards have contributed to the career development of 20 talented Australian artists and over $600,000 in award prizes.

Regarding my hatched: For the past 34 years, Hatched has recognised and celebrated the most promising and diverse practices of recent tertiary art graduates, selected for their creative excellence and unique modes of expression—many of whom have gone on to gain recognition later in their careers. This digital archive offers a space to reflect on and celebrate the rich legacy of the Hatched: National Graduate Show , while showcasing the creative pathways and possibilities that may lie ahead for the future generations of emerging artists. This site profiles a snapshot of Hatched alumni, highlighting the diversity of practices, disciplines and stories that contribute to and shape Australian contemporary art in profound and exciting ways—demonstrating Hatched’s enduring impact on the national arts landscape.
Regarding my hatched: 51 James Street Perth Cultural Centre Perth, WA 6000 + 61 (0) 8 9228 6300 info@pica.org.au

Regarding my judy wheeler: The Judy Wheeler Commission was established to honour the legacy of Judy Wheeler, an enduring lover and supporter of the arts. Established by Judy Wheeler’s husband Jamie and children Tom and Genevieve Simpson, the Commission supports artists from across Australia to create bold new work that responds to PICA’s architecture and history as one of Perth’s first schools and now a contemporary art space.

Regarding my judy wheeler: Selected from an annual open call, artists are encouraged to match PICA’s spirit of risk and experimentation in their proposals, addressing spaces that PICA’s visitors move through when visiting the building, including its entrance lobby, foyer, stairwells and balcony mezzanine. Each commission includes an artist fee of $10,000 and is installed for up to a one-year period.

Regarding my judy wheeler: Judy Wheeler was born in 1954 and grew up in Gosford, New South Wales. She spent a year at the National Institute of Dramatic Art, obtained a teaching diploma at Sydney Teachers College and a Bachelor of Arts from Flinders University. She later worked as a town councillor and bookshop owner. Throughout her life she was an enduring lover and supporter of the arts. For several years she funded Western Australia’s T.A.G. Hungerford literary award, and through her patronage of the visual arts she amassed a substantial collection of Australian prints and paintings. She passed away in 2010 after a long illness.

Regarding my boorda yeyi: boorda yeyi, meaning ‘future now’ in Whadjuk Noongar language, is Australia’s first pathway program for artists seeking to work with immersive technologies. Launched in 2025 by PICA, it explores how technology can deepen artistic ideas and transform the way audiences experience contemporary art— bridging spatial and sensory boundaries to create encounters that are felt, not just seen.

Regarding my boorda yeyi: In 2026, all streams return. Artists can submit an expression of interest to attend the second Foundational Symposium, participate in an Intensive Mentorship, or apply for the next Immersive Arts Commission.

Regarding my boorda yeyi: April Phillips, the inaugural recipient of the Immersive Arts Commission in 2025, premieres her work Under Waters at PICA in February 2026 before touring later in the year. This immersive installation invites audiences into a responsive oceanic environment, weaving extended reality with First Nations knowledge systems to explore interdependence and care in a time of climate crisis.

Regarding my boorda yeyi: Immersive art is not about technology for its own sake—it’s about expanding the language of art to create experiences that challenge perception, evoke emotion and invite participation. Through boorda yeyi , PICA stands at the forefront of this evolution, championing originality, artistic excellence and critical depth. Join us as we imagine what art can be when boundaries dissolve and futures unfold, now.
Regarding my boorda yeyi: The program name, boorda yeyi , was developed in consultation with Whadjuk Elder, Dr Richard Walley OAM, and Whadjuk members of PICA’s Aboriginal Advisory Group.

Regarding my support: We need the support of individuals like you who share our values, our sense of adventure and our desire to create career-defining moments for artists and life-enhancing experiences for audiences.
Regarding my support: PICA is a not-for-profit organisation registered with The Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC). All donations $2 or more are tax-deductible.

Regarding my support: At PICA we believe that contemporary artists are the trailblazers, innovators and change-makers that give us a glimpse of what is possible. In acknowledgement of this, we work hard to make contemporary arts experiences accessible and engaging to diverse communities, while championing radical new art practices and embracing challenging subject matter that fosters awareness and understanding.

Regarding my support: Put your appreciation of art and artists, and your belief in their positive impact on people and communities, into action through PICA. Becoming a PICA Donor is a simple yet powerful way to express your support for contemporary art and keep PICA free for everyone.
Regarding my support: If you would like to discuss your giving options please contact Anne Tunnecliffe, PICA’s Development Manager, at philanthropy@pica.org.au or 08 9228 6300

Regarding my support: Put simply, philanthropy means ‘love of humanity’. If you believe art benefits us all and should be freely available to everyone, give what you can and become an Instant Philanthropist. Every dollar makes a difference and any amount over $2 is tax deductible.

Regarding my support: Join PICA’s award-winning annual giving program as an Art 1000 Donor ( $1,250 ), Art Ambassador ( $2,500 ) or Director’s Circle Donor ( $5,500 ). Direct your donation to a vital program area, see the outcomes of your support and be kept up to date on your impact.

Regarding my support: Multi-year investments through our Art Commissioners make it possible for PICA to commit to long-range engagement with artists and nurture them every step of the way – from first concept to final presentation. Through this critical support, artists can take the next big leap in their practice and bring their most ambitious ideas to life. Art Commissioners donate $10,500 or more per year over three years and closely follow their supported projects, forming personal connections with commissioned artists.

Regarding my support: PICA is honoured to have the trust and belief of so many dedicated people, or as we think of them – friends. Our Donor Champions are passionate individuals who have volunteered to advocate the important role PICA plays in the arts and culture landscape and to help you make a deep and personal connection with our work.

Regarding my support: ‘ Being involved in the Commissioning Fund has been a truly rewarding experience. For me, helping to provide the means to access the essential tools and people for the development of a creative work and then witnessing the result, is exceptionally gratifying. I love the fact that PICA pushes creative boundaries and the result is always surprising, poignant and thoroughly entertaining. ‘

Regarding my support: ‘Having immersed myself in contemporary art here in Perth I was drawn to the invaluable support PICA provides for artists evolving their practice locally, throughout Australia and overseas. In this way, PICA is critical to the development of our arts and culture. My passion is diving into the artists’ practice and communicating this to those already avid collecting and those who are looking to begin their collecting journey. It is important we encourage new people to attend the many exhibitions, artists talks and residencies facilitated by PICA to provide increased awareness of and support to so many talented artists. I am committed to raising awareness about PICA’s incredible work. ‘

Regarding my support: ‘I still recall the moment I decided to support PICA and be part of its journey. It was during a conversation with PICA’s Philanthropy Manager where she explained the extensive work PICA does with contemporary artists, often over several years. This thoughtful and sustained approach truly resonated with me, and I knew I wanted to be a part of it. As an Art 1000 donor, our donations are directed towards the Hatched: National Graduate Show which supports emerging artists by offering them a platform to exhibit their work, gain industry exposure, and receive valuable professional development. It’s been thrilling to watch their careers blossom, with many achieving national and international recognition, and feeling, in some small way, a part of their journey. ‘

Regarding my bequest: A bequest is a deeply meaningful and enduring way to share your love of the arts. By leaving a gift in your Will to PICA you can contribute to shaping WA arts and culture for generations to come. We welcome the opportunity to discuss your bequest with you, how we can recognise your generosity during your lifetime and honour your legacy into the future.
Regarding my bequest: PICA accepts gifts of cash, assets, property or shares with funds directed to our areas of greatest need to sustain our work and impact.
Regarding my bequest: To leave a bequest to PICA please quote our ABN in your Will and clearly state the amount, percentage of your estate or the intended gift you would like to give.
Regarding my bequest: In addition to reaching out to us, we recommend you discuss your intentions with your financial planner or solicitor, your executor and/or your family.

Regarding my bequest: Create a legacy during your lifetime or in honour of a loved one and inspire artists and audiences for years to come. As a multi-arts organisation for people of all ages and stages of life, PICA offers a wide range of programs from artistic residencies, performances, exhibitions and large commissioning works to community engagement and student learning programs. We also provide career pathways for emerging arts workers to build a skilled and talented workforce that understands and supports local arts. By working with us to plan a major gift that helps us to achieve our strategic goals you will create something special for the community that celebrates you or your loved one’s love of arts and culture.

Regarding my bequest: If you are considering a bequest or legacy gift we invite you to have a confidential discussion and explore your options at PICA with Anne Tunnecliffe, PICA’s Development Manager, at philanthropy@pica.org.au or 08 9228 6300.

Regarding my bequest: The Judy Wheeler Commission is a 10-year site-specific commissioning program in memory of the late Judy Wheeler, gifted to PICA by her loving family – husband Jamie and children Genevieve and Thomas.

Regarding my bequest: Their significant gift of $300,000, the largest in PICA’s history, enables the 12-month display of a commissioned work by an Australian visual artist that responds physically or conceptually to the architecture and history of the PICA building and embodies PICA’s spirit of risk and experimentation.

Regarding my bequest: ‘One thing that has always stood out to me about PICA is its efficiency. It puts on quality exhibitions despite only having a small number of staff, at least relative to most other galleries . I also think the scale of the donation felt like a good match for PICA in that it was an amount that was meaningful yet still likely to be manageable. I’m really looking forward to seeing what eventuates from this Commission, especially 10 years from now when there’s a substantial body of work to look back on.’ – Thomas Simpson

Regarding my bequest: In 2023, Meanjin (Brisbane) based artist Elizabeth Willing was the inaugural Judy Wheeler Commission artist and delivered Roost – a sensory work across mediums that enveloped PICA’s foyer and stairwell. Learn more about the Judy Wheeler Commission .

Regarding my impact: PICA is a registered not-for-profit entity that has proudly served WA’s arts-loving community since 1991. More than 100,000 people pass through our doors each year, including over 7,000 school students of all ages, to experience exhibitions, performances, studio programs, creative learning workshops and more.

Regarding my impact: We are in awe of our passionate donors and partners. Every dollar they give goes towards making our work possible. Below is a snapshot of the collective good created because of their support.
Regarding my impact: Donate today or to find out more about the impact donations and partnerships make at PICA please contact Anne Tunnecliffe at philanthropy@pica.org.au or 08 9228 6300
Regarding my impact: ‘I absolutely loved the training session about Vision Awareness and community accessibility. It made me think about my practice and how accessible I can make it.’
Regarding my impact: ‘It was great to be part of Hatched. I enjoyed meeting and sharing experiences with all the artists, talking about their practice and the show.’

Regarding my impact: The image above is of the 2023 cohort of Hatched artists – the people who have directly benefited from the support of PICA’s Art 1000 donors. Hatched is the only national survey of newly graduated art students in Australia and is a celebration of fresh and diverse perspectives from the rising stars of Australian contemporary art.

Regarding my impact: In addition to the exhibition, Art 1000 donations enabled PICA to create a program of bespoke artist-focused professional development activities for the exhibition artists. This includes talks, workshops, a symposium and training that provides vital opportunities for the artists to learn more about professional practice at this crucial early stage of their careers.
Regarding my impact: In 2023, 22 of the 26 exhibiting artists from around the country converged on Perth for the opening night.

Regarding my impact: ‘I loved how Hatched showcases every artist’s individuality. It’s so different yet the exhibition is still so cohesive.’ ‘I liked the variety of artworks and the children’s activity is excellent.’

Regarding my impact: ‘The history of PICA deserves risks to be taken and those risks can only be taken when there is a feeling of support. It was a great honour to swim around in PICA’s archives and to test myself after twenty years of practice. I feel much more confident in my work knowing I was supported to achieve my vision. It was an honour to work with PICA in this way.’

Regarding my impact: A major gift by the Ungar Family Foundation provided PICA with the opportunity to take a bold step in 2024 and commission one of Australia’s most famous artists, Agatha Gothe-Snape, to transform our once black box performance space into a sunlit and welcoming foyer space.

Regarding my impact: Agatha spent time deep-diving into PICA’s archives and in close conversation with our current and past staff to draw inspiration for this major new site-specific commission. Her unique ability to engage with people and place enabled her to distil PICA’s 30-plus years of relationships, history and programming into a single space that holds many stories and welcomes many experiences.

Regarding my impact: ‘I’m grateful to PICA’s Art Commissioners for their generous donations that make PICA’s commissioning program possible. Their support allows interesting stories to be told and really strengthens the impact of our creative community. ‘I get people to navigate through my work in a wheelchair to give them a little vignette of what people like myself have to navigate on a daily basis. What really interests me is how you can change minds with something that is fleeting. I’m hoping people are becoming more empathetic to people who are different to themselves.’

Regarding my impact: In 2023, through donations made by PICA’s Art Commissioners , artist Bruno Booth took over the Perth Cultural Centre amphitheatre with his work Dead Ends and Detours and put audiences in wheelchairs to demonstrate that ‘disability’ is not a dirty word . Mixing sculpture, sport, urban design and disability aesthetics, more than 600 people participated in the installation over a weekend with Bruno offering participants a direct insight into the lived experience of physical disability and the navigational challenges he faces as a wheelchair user.

Regarding my impact: ‘From the PICA residency I learnt that I could do this – not just from a creative and professional perspective but from a physical one too. ‘That my condition will not limit me, but now informs my practice and the type of work I strive to create.’

Regarding my impact: Sarah Nelson is an actor, puppeteer, mask/physical performer and maker across theatre, film and community arts who participated in a three-week residency at PICA as part of PICA’s Studio Program. The Studio Program is supported by donations from PICA’s Art Ambassadors and provides artists with a dedicated space to nurture their practice.
Regarding my impact: Artists are invited to embark on new projects, connect with a creative community, find new audiences and gain critical feedback on their work.

Regarding my impact: Sarah’s theatre work in development, Into the Fog , was inspired by her experience of living in the UK during prolonged isolation with long COVID and her subsequent development of FND (Functional Neurological Disorder).
